# Data Management and Sharing Plan

<!-- REQUIRED for all NIH applications generating scientific data (DMS Policy,
     effective 2023-01-25). Recommended limit: 2 pages. Use NIH's six required
     elements as the headings below — reviewers and program staff check for
     them by name, so do not rename or reorder them.
     Costs for data management belong in the Budget Justification. -->

## 1. Data Type

Types, amount, and format of scientific data to be generated and which will be
preserved and shared. Distinguish raw from processed data, and state what will
*not* be shared and why.

## 2. Related Tools, Software and/or Code

Whether specialized tools are needed to access or analyze the data, and how
they will be made available (e.g. an open-source repository under a stated
license).

## 3. Standards

Data standards, formats, and metadata vocabularies to be applied, so the data
are interpretable by others.

## 4. Data Preservation, Access, and Associated Timelines

- **Repository.** Name it, and prefer an NIH-designated or discipline-specific
  one where a relevant repository exists.
- **Identifiers.** Persistent identifiers (DOI/accession) enabling findability.
- **Timeline.** When data become available and how long they persist. No later
  than publication or end of the award period, whichever comes first.

## 5. Access, Distribution, or Reuse Considerations

Applicable factors limiting reuse: informed consent, privacy and protection of
identifiable information, and any other restrictions. Controlled-access
justification, if applicable.

## 6. Oversight of Data Management and Sharing

Who is responsible (by role and name), and how compliance is monitored across
the award.
